findings.evidence: The function comment says the input is the approved partial refund amount, but the new gateway call uses the full order total instead, so any caller requesting a smaller refund will overpay the customer.
findings.recommendation: Pass the approved refund amount through to the gateway call, e.g. use amount_cents here, and add a test covering a partial refund where amount_cents is less than order.total_cents.

findings.title: Partial refund now issues a full-total refund to the customer
findings.evidence: The added call passes order.total_cents instead of the caller-supplied amount_cents: '    return gateway.refund(order.txn_id, order.total_cents)'. Reachable path: a support agent approves a partial amount (the documented contract of the amount_cents parameter) and calls refund(order, partial_cents); the gateway is instructed to return the entire order total, irreversibly overpaying the customer and leaking money on every partial-refund request.
findings.recommendation: Restore the caller-supplied amount: 'return gateway.refund(order.txn_id, amount_cents)'. Add an explicit guard that 0 < amount_cents <= order.total_cents and reject/clamp otherwise, so the parameter cannot silently diverge from the payout.

findings.title: TOCTOU check-then-open loses atomic claim and can truncate a concurrently created file
findings.evidence: After the separate exists check on line 11, the new branch opens the path in write mode, so two concurrent claim_path calls for the same name can both pass the check and the second open truncates the first caller's file; the previous open(path, x) was atomic.
findings.recommendation: Keep the atomic exclusive create by returning open(path, 'x') and letting it raise FileExistsError, or use os.open(path, os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_WRONLY). Do not rely on a prior exists check.

findings.title: Check-then-open introduces a race that can overwrite a concurrently created file
findings.evidence: The new code first checks 'os.path.exists(path)' and then opens the same path with write mode, so another process or thread can create the file after the check but before 'open(path, 'w')'. In that reachable interleaving on POSIX, this call truncates the newly created file instead of raising FileExistsError as before.
findings.recommendation: Keep the atomic exclusive-create behavior by using 'open(path, 'x')' directly, or use an equivalent os.open call with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and then wrap it in a file object.

findings.title: AWS access key hardcoded in deploy script
findings.evidence: A new module-level constant assigns a literal credential: 'AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID = "[REDACTED-AWS-KEY]"' with no env lookup or secret-manager fetch. Every clone, CI log, artifact, or code review of this repo exposes a live deploy credential; anyone with read access to the repository can deploy to the account until the key is revoked, and revocation requires a code change plus rotation of anything already cached.
findings.recommendation: Remove the literal and revoke/rotate the key immediately. Read credentials from the standard provider chain (AWS_PROFILE, instance role, or SSO) or from an env var / secrets manager at runtime, e.g. os.environ or boto3.Session(). Fail fast with a clear error if no credential is available, and add a secret-scanning check (git-secrets / CI regex) so this cannot be re-introduced.

findings.title: Unparameterized execute: any term with a single quote raises a DB error (500)
findings.evidence: The new 'return db.execute(q)' passes no parameter binding, so a perfectly normal search for a name like O'Brien produces the malformed statement 'SELECT * FROM docs WHERE title LIKE '%O'Brien%'' and SQLite raises a syntax error. The previous call 'db.execute(q, (f"%{term}%",))' let the driver quote the value. This turns an ordinary user input into an exception on every request containing an apostrophe, which will surface as 500s and error-log noise in production.
findings.recommendation: Restore parameter binding so the value is quoted by the driver; if the raw form must stay, the code needs explicit escaping plus try/except around execute to convert driver errors into a handled search failure rather than an unhandled 500.
